name: Project Tijuana
description: Project Tijuana partners with underserved communities just south of the US-Mexico border to design and implement sustainable water access and civil infrastructure. Our team works directly with community members to ensure solutions are locally owned and maintained long after our involvement ends.

timeline.title: Community Assessment
timeline.description: Conducted initial site visits and community needs assessment with local partners.

timeline.title: Design Phase
timeline.description: Completed engineering design for water distribution system.

timeline.title: Implementation Begins
timeline.description: Ground broke on the first phase of the water distribution project.

timeline.title: Phase 1 Complete
timeline.description: First distribution line serving 40 households successfully commissioned.

name: Project Kachieng
description: Project Kachieng works with the Kachieng community in rural Kenya to address critical infrastructure needs including clean water access, sanitation, and structural improvements. Our chapter collaborates with EWB-USA professional mentors and local community leaders to ensure every solution is appropriate, sustainable, and community-driven.

timeline.title: Project Initiation
timeline.description: Formal partnership established with the Kachieng community.

timeline.title: Assessment Trip
timeline.description: Team traveled to Kenya to conduct on-site water quality and infrastructure assessment.

timeline.title: Design Complete
timeline.description: Borehole and hand pump system design finalized and approved by EWB-USA.

timeline.title: Implementation Trip
timeline.description: Team successfully installed borehole pump serving over 300 community members.

name: Project K-12
tagline: STEM outreach for San Diego students.
description: Project K-12 brings hands-on engineering education to San Diego area K-12 students, with a focus on underserved schools and underrepresented communities. Through workshops, mentorship, and design challenges, we inspire the next generation of engineers and show students from all backgrounds that engineering is for them.

timeline.title: Program Launch
timeline.description: Partnered with two San Diego Unified schools for pilot STEM workshop series.

timeline.title: Curriculum Developed
timeline.description: Created six-module engineering curriculum covering water, energy, and structures.

timeline.title: Expansion
timeline.description: Expanded to four schools, reaching over 200 students across the semester.

timeline.title: Design Challenge Event
timeline.description: Hosted first annual EWB-UCSD Engineering Design Challenge with 80 student participants.
